### Non-obvious logic and implementation notes

1. **Person Navigator ("Person 2 of 9"):** This requires the parent list view to pass the ordered set of person IDs (from the current smart list or search) into the detail view. Arrow navigation uses this array to jump to adjacent records without returning to the list. The keyboard shortcuts (← →) are registered globally on the detail view. The total count "9" comes from the source list's filtered result count.

2. **Email tracking pixel in timeline:** The body preview shows the pixel URL inline — FUB appears to store the raw email body text as sent (including the tracking parameter appended to the website URL). The display truncates at a certain character count with "..." The `_pxl` parameter is a base64 or encoded identifier that FUB's tracking server uses to log open events. The "3 opens" badge is a count of how many times that pixel was loaded.

3. **"via automation" label:** Each timeline email event shows the channel. When the email was sent by an automation sequence (drip), this label appears. Manually sent emails would not show this label.

4. **Overdue task styling:** The only visual distinction for an overdue task is the due date text rendered in red. There is no banner, no section highlight, no card background change — just the color of the timestamp.

5. **"Running" automation status:** Uses a green dot (`●`) + "Running" text. The pause button (‖) is inline to the right. This suggests a simple enum: running → paused → completed. The automation name "Web Inquiry Option 01" is the FUB action plan / drip sequence name configured in the Admin panel.

6. **Email signature is pre-rendered:** The signature block appears fully rendered inside the compose area (photo + formatted text + logo + links) before any body text is typed. This is FUB's auto-appended signature feature — users configure their signature in profile settings and it auto-inserts into every email compose.

7. **Template chips:** The chips ("Introduction", "Follow Up", "Still Buying", "Nurture Lead", "+ Custom") are quick-insert buttons. Clicking one likely populates both the Subject and Body with a pre-written template. The templates shown are likely the FUB-provided default templates or user-customized ones. "Still Buying" is specific to a buyer-lead nurture context.

8. **AgentFire FUB Widget:** This is a third-party integration (AgentFire = a real-estate IDX website platform). The widget section is collapsed but present in every person record — it shows the contact's website activity from AgentFire (pages visited, properties saved, searches run). Third-party integrations appear as named collapsible sections in the right sidebar.

9. **Collaborators vs Assigned Agent:** FUB distinguishes between the primary assigned agent and collaborators. Collaborators can view and interact with the record but the primary agent "owns" it for reporting purposes.

10. **"Seen 17 days ago":** This "Activity" section header with the "Seen X ago" label is FUB's website tracking feature — it shows when this lead last visited the brokerage website (tracked via the `_pxl` pixel). The dropdown (▼) may show a history of visit sessions.

11. **BCC toggle:** The BCC field is hidden by default; only "Cc" is shown. A "BCC" link appears at the right end of the Cc row that, when clicked, adds a third field row for BCC recipients.

12. **Attachments/Templates tabs in compose:** These appear below the rich text editor but above the footer. They toggle between showing an attachment file picker panel and a template search panel within the compose area, without closing or losing the compose state.
